Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Gaurav Nagpal, learned counsel
for the petitioner.
2. Ms. Sweta Badola Dobhal, learned
Brief Holder for the State.
3. Petitioners have impugned the FIR
No.0487 of 2026 lodged under Sections
8/20/21/27(a)/29 of the NDPS Act at
P.S. Rishikesh, District Dehradun.
4. As per the FIR, the police party, on
25.09.2026 at about 15:10 hours, found
2-3 persons standing next to a blue
colour car which was parked about 50
paces away trenching ground from the
forest road. When police party reached
towards them, two persons ran away
with the car while one person named
Gurcharan @ Munna S/o late Subhash
(petitioner no.3) was arrested, and he
was found having 435 gram of Charas
and 14.5 gram of smack in his

UKHC010181242026
2026:UHC:9590
possession. On interrogation, he
submitted that persons who were
travelling in the car had possessed rest
of contraband. On the basis of said
statement, first information report was
lodged against Gurcharan Singh @
Munna. Subsequently during
investigation, names of petitioner nos. 1
and 2 have come up on the basis of the
statement of the petitioner no.3. The
petitioners are before this Court seeking
quashing of the impugned FIR.
6. This Court vide order dated
12.10.2026 had called upon the State
Counsel to get instructions in the matter
specifically regarding the role of
petitioners no. 1 and 2 in the impugned
FIR.
7. Today, on instructions, the learned
State Counsel submits that against
petitioner no.1, there are 11 cases
registered; though there is no criminal
case was found registered against the
petitioner no.2 yet, but it is reported
that these persons are indulged in cases
of NDPS Act.
8. Having perused the impugned FIR,
it is prima facie reflected that cases

UKHC010181242026
2026:UHC:9590
under the NDPS Act are made against
the petitioners. Moreover, it has time
and again been held that the FIR cannot
be an encyclopedia. But during
investigation, name of petitioner no.1
and 2 have cropped up.
9. Looking to the seriousness of the
offences alleged against the petitioners,
no case for setting aside the impugned
FIR is made out.
10. Accordingly, the writ petition is
dismissed.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 26.10.2026
